title: mia-li-oncall-scratchpad-2026-03-04
content:
On-call scratchpad — 2026-03-04
Owner: Mia Li (eng-sre)
Summary / timeline:
- 02:12 AM: Pager — high p95/p99 latency for hosted API (text-generation route) in us-west1.
- 02:14 AM: Confirmed increased tail latencies across multiple model routes (gpt-4-like, gpt-3.5x). Error rate stable but token Latency spiked.
- 02:20 AM: Correlated with a recent deploy to infra-config (cache rotation change) rolled out at 01:56 AM.
- 02:28 AM: Mitigation applied — rolled back cache-rotation config on cdn-config service. Began manual cache-warm for top 20 prefixes.
- 02:40 AM: Latency returning to baseline; p99 dropped from ~2.3s to ~450ms over next 30m.
- 03:15 AM: Pager resolved. Monitoring set to watch for recurrence.

Initial hypothesis:
- Cache key rotation introduced incompatibility with existing prefix hashing; caused a large-scale cache miss storm (many requests forced to origin / GPU warm paths).
- Not a model issue (gpu utilization did increase but no OOMs); main cost was increased token compute from cold starts.

Actions taken during incident:
- Rolled back infra-config change (PR ref in linked artifacts).
- Manual cache-warm for top traffic prefixes (commands: curl seq + warm endpoint — notes in incident channel).
- Increased autoscale target for dedicated pool to absorb burst for 20m while we stabilized.
- Notified CS on impacted customers (internal ticket INC-2026-0421).

Immediate follow-ups (short-term):
- [ ] Add alert for abnormal cache miss ratio: cache_miss_rate > 5% sustained for 5m (owner: Priya, due: 2026-03-07).
- [ ] Harden deploy gating: include canary for cache rotation changes (owner: Samir, due: 2026-03-14).
- [ ] Update Cache Eviction/Rotation runbook with specific rollback steps and test checklist (owner: Mia, due: 2026-03-06).
- [ ] Add automated cache-warm job for top N prefixes after rotation (owner: infra team, contact: @infra-oncall).

Longer-term / backlog items (postmortem TODOs):
- [ ] Run a chaos test for cache key rotations in staging and dedicated envs (owner: eng-sre + serving-runtime).
- [ ] Evaluate adaptive TTL strategy to reduce cold-start spikes for high-traffic prefixes.
- [ ] Add telemetry to track which prefixes see the highest cold-start cost per minute (cost attribution).
- [ ] Update runbooks for every feature that touches cache key format with mandatory integration tests.

Notes to self / rough commands used while troubleshooting:
- grep logs: gcloud logging read 'resource.type="http_load_balancer" AND jsonPayload.route="/v1/generate"' --limit 200
- warm script (used): scripts/warm_prefixes.sh top-prefixes-20 --concurrency 8
- rollback: kubectl set image deploy/cdn-config cdn-config=redwood/cdn-config:2026-02-18-rollback && kubectl rollout status deploy/cdn-config -n infra

Communications / stakeholders:
- Notified on-call PM and duty manager at 02:30 AM.
- Customer Success notified for top 3 affected customers — follow-up email drafted, waiting on ops sign-off.

Questions / open uncertainties:
- Why was the rotation not caught by existing predeploy checks? (Need to review CI gating for config format changes.)
- Are we confident warm script covers all relevant prefixes (edge-case: dynamic prefixes from user-specific routing)?

SRE runbook TODO checklist (short):
- [ ] Add explicit step: validate new cache key format against previous live keyset (unit test + integration).
- [ ] Add safety net: if cache miss rate > threshold for 2 minutes, auto-roll back config.
- [ ] Document manual warm process with exact command examples and target concurrency.

Post-incident: create postmortem draft (owner: Mia) — include timeline, RCA, impact metrics (rps, p99 before/after, cost estimate for extra GPU time). Draft target: 2026-03-08.

Misc notes (scratchy):
- Remember to ping infra-automation about adding a dry-run for rotation to staging tenant.
- Check storage-level TTLs for embedding caches too (we saw a smaller bump in embedding route at 02:18).
- Log a retro item for on-call run: improve runbook access (confluence links in runbook header).

End of scratchpad.
